resistance_detail.note: The pulmonary arterial-to-venous path spans pulmonary arteries, arterioles, capillaries, venules and veins. In isolated dog lung lobes, arteries, capillaries and veins accounted for 46/34/20% of total lobar vascular resistance, and pulmonary arteries for approximately 50% of resistance upstream of the sluice point when alveolar pressure exceeded venous pressure; a review reports preparation-dependent pressure-drop shares of 30±7/17±3/39±13% (sum 86%, remainder unexplained). These cited preparations and conditions do not show resistance concentrated in one segment, but they do not establish the distribution generally, in vivo, or in humans. Annotation only; the model does not resolve these segments.

resistance_detail.note: The systemic arterial-to-venous path spans arteries, small arteries, arterioles, capillaries, venules and veins. The sources give pressure-drop shares, not measured resistance shares: a review reports the muscular small arteries and arterioles account for 70% of the pressure drop, and capillaries and veins 7% and 19% (systemic data attributed there to mesenteric and skeletal-muscle beds), and a hamster cheek-pouch study reports 50% of the total pressure drop across that bed in small cheek pouch arteries. Equating pressure-drop shares with resistance shares requires equal flow through segments in series; this is an assumption, not a measurement, and does not give a whole-system or human resistance fraction across parallel beds. Annotation only; the model does not resolve these segments.
